featureNouns.guidance: Extract subsystem and capability nouns from the title and description after removing stopwords. Prefer multi-word phrases over single tokens: 'branch tracker' finds more than 'branch'. Include command names, metadata file names, and any identifier written in code formatting.

targetFiles.guidance: Independently of the description's vocabulary, ask which files a change of this shape would modify, then search for other work touching those same files — open and closed issues, and the files themselves. Treat each derived path as a search term in its own right.
targetFiles.rationale: Feature-noun extraction misses prior work that shares no vocabulary with the request. Worked example: #2516 restructures review-criteria.json and its schema; #2517 adds a criterion to the same file. A sweep on the words 'prior art' surfaces neither from the other; a sweep on 'what files would this touch' surfaces it immediately.

signals: Implementing code exists and is reachable from a documented entry point
A closed issue describes the same capability and its acceptance criteria are checked
A command spec, rule, or reference document already specifies the behavior
The capability is listed in CHANGELOG.md under a released version
alreadyShipped.action: STOP without creating the artifact. Report the conflicting issue numbers and file paths.

signals: Related work exists but addresses a different surface, path, or actor
Prior implementation was reverted, deprecated, or superseded
Prior issue was closed without implementation
Existing capability is a subset and the request extends it
Existing work is in another repository in the ecosystem
warranted.action: Continue. Record a Prior Art section listing what exists and how the new work differs.

signals: No matching code, spec, test, or metadata on any resolved surface
No matching issue title or body across open and closed issues
noneFound.action: Continue. Record the none-found line, including the terms searched.

bodyFormat.heading: **Prior Art:**
bodyFormat._recognisedFormsNote: RECOGNITION vs EMISSION (#2700). The formats below are what the commands EMIT. Detection accepts more: a hand-written markdown heading counts too, so an author who writes ## Prior Art is not reported as having skipped the sweep. heading above is the emitted form only — reading it as the sole accepted form is the misreading #2700 fixed.
bodyFormat.partialFormat: **Prior Art:** PARTIAL — <what ran>; <what failed and why>

questions.question: Does this capability already exist in the codebase, in whole or in part?
questions.guidance: Search resolved surfaces for implementing code, specs, metadata, and tests. A partial match still matters — record which part exists.
questions.actionIfFound: Classify against dispositions. Fully present and reachable maps to already-shipped; a subset maps to found-but-warranted.

questions.question: Has this been filed before, including as a closed issue?
questions.guidance: Search issue history with includeClosed. Titles frequently share no vocabulary with the request, so search derived target-file paths as well as feature nouns.
questions.actionIfFound: List the issue numbers and their relationship. A closed-without-implementation issue is found-but-warranted, not already-shipped.

questions.question: What other in-flight work touches the files this change would modify?
questions.guidance: Derive target files per termDerivation.targetFiles, then search open issues for those paths. This is the axis that finds interdependence a vocabulary search cannot.
questions.actionIfFound: Record the overlap and note which issue should land first, or that whichever lands second rebases.

questions.question: Does this belong to, or duplicate, work in a companion repository?
questions.guidance: Check whether the capability is owned elsewhere in the ecosystem before specifying it here.
questions.actionIfFound: Record the owning repository. Out-of-scope work maps to already-shipped for this repo's purposes.
